title: Public structs with exhaustive fields missing #[non_exhaustive]
description:
Public structs with all-public fields allow callers to construct them using struct literal syntax (`Struct { field: val, .. }`). Adding any field later breaks all such construction sites.

**Locations:**
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/error.rs:7` - `BufferTooSmall`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/error.rs:24` - `TooShort`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/compress.rs:52` - `FieldDescriptor`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/compress.rs:78` - `Rule`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/wire.rs:237` - `Fragment`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/wire.rs:465` - `Ack`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/wire.rs:646` - `Ack128`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/no_ack.rs:165` - `NoAckResult`
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/ack_on_error.rs:601` - `ReceiverResult`

**What goes wrong:** If we need to add a field (e.g., `BufferTooSmall.hint: Option<&'static str>` for better error messages, or `Fragment.integrity_code` for future RFC extensions), every caller constructing these types with struct literals breaks. This is common for test fixtures: `Fragment { rule_id: 0, dtag: 0, window: 0, fcn: 1, payload: &[0], rcs: [0;4] }`.

**Fix:** Add `#[non_exhaustive]` and provide constructor functions (`BufferTooSmall::new(needed, available)`, `Fragment::new(...)`) as the stable API. Existing test code in-crate is fine; external callers must migrate to constructors.
close_reason: Added #[non_exhaustive] to Fragment, Ack, Ack128, Control in wire.rs
